newsitem.title: UK: Ldn gold fixes at new recent low on IMF news.
newsitem.headline: Ldn gold fixes at new recent low on IMF news.

text.p: Gold prices slumped on Thursday afternoon after news the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had the necessary majority to sell five million ounces of gold from its reserves.
Gold was fixed at $380.45 after $382.05 this morning. It was the lowest gold fix since September 6, 1995. It closed at $380.15 compared with $382.65 on Wednesday.
The low fix followed a statement from IMF managing director Michel Camdessus that the organisation had a majority in favour of selling gold to help the world's poorest nations.

He also said he was unsure of the timing of the sale and that it would only be done if the IMF member countries could not come up with the necessary funding to get the new assistance programme under way.

Earlier selling by the mainly U.S.-owned investment funds had put pressure on prices as fund managers became disillusioned by gold's lustreless price performance compared with soaring prices on the stock and bond markets.
The prospect of the IMF selling gold has been hovering over the market for several weeks and weas cited as a major factor restraining interest in gold recently.
One dealer commented, "Yes it has been a factor, but the last time the IMF sold gold (in the late 1970s) the price actually went up."
Dealers said the volume involved was not a problem for the market to absorb but the signal sent to central bank and other gold holders could be seen inviting further sales of reserves.

"It (the IMF sale) will be over a long period and well organised and it has been discounted into the price already. What we saw today was people just taking a last minute punt at it," said one dealer.
Even so, the dealer added that the gold price was targetted at $378.00 now. Once it fell that far, some dealers were forecasting a bounce back up to $383.00.
Platinum recorded its lowest fixing since January 31, 1994 at $385.25 per ounce beating its previous recent low on September 23 of $386.50, the lowest since April 20, 1994.
The fixing session took 35 minutes -- its usually over in less than five minutes -- and after a couple of good sellers came in, selling spread rapidly, dealers said.
Platinum has been under pressure since it fell down through $390.00 earlier this month.
Dealers said consumers were content to live off their stocks while the market was apparently oversupplied and weakening.
Platinum closed at $385.50 down from $388.00 on Wednesday.
Silver and palladium were relatively unscathed by the falls in gold and platinum although both of them have looked weak and friendless recently.
Silver finished at $4.89 down three cents from the previous close and palladium was at $117.75, down $1.50.
